title: Aurora, the Day-Spring
author: Jakob Bohme (Sparrow trans)
description: Aurora (Morgenröte im Aufgang, 'The Day-Spring or Morning Redness in the Rising of the Sun') by Jakob Böhme (1575-1624), the Lutheran shoemaker-mystic of Görlitz, in the seventeenth-century English translation by John Sparrow (1656), edited in modern reprints by C. J. Barker and D. S. Hehner. Written in 1612 after a visionary illumination, it is Böhme's first book, and its circulation led to his being forbidden to write by the local pastor. It describes 'the root or mother of philosophy, astrology and theology' through an account of God's nature as dynamic interplay of qualities or 'source-spirits', the Trinity, the creation and fall of the angels and Lucifer, and the origin of good and evil, the heavens, the stars and the elements. Dense and visionary, it founded the theosophical tradition that influenced German Idealism, Romanticism, William Law, Blake and later Christian esotericism.
